transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Perez (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Nebula - Head of ML), Lena Ortiz (Nebula - Infra), Tom Wu (Nebula - Security), Rae Kim (Nebula - PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Alright hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this deal, and with me is Maya, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Samir: Good, thanks. Busy week but good to be here.
[00:12] Maya: Hey all. Today we want to take you through the Console tracing features, error analysis, request logs and how to debug a failing pipeline. We'll try to keep it practical — show a couple of real examples and then leave time for Qs.
[00:25] Rae: Perfect, that's what we asked for. We're mostly interested in reproducibility and auditability; Tom will pepper with security questions.
[00:34] Tom: Yep, mainly around retention, KMS, and who can see logs.
[00:38] Jordan: Great, we'll cover RBAC and masking in the security section as part of request logs. Maya, want to share your screen?
[00:46] Maya: Sure, sharing now. Tell me if you see the Console.
[00:50] Lena: We can see it. The tracing page looks familiar from the doc.
[00:55] Maya: Cool. So top-level, the tracing view correlates requests across services — you can see per-request latency, error type, model variant, and routing decisions. This is a live project scoped to a demo dataset.
[01:10] Maya: If we click into a failed request, the right pane shows the request-log (raw prompt, truncated tokens), the model response, and the kernel/runtime events: batching, cache hits/misses, and fallback chains.
[01:22] Samir: Quick question — does that include KV cache metrics? We use a lot of multi-turn chat, so cache behavior matters.
[01:29] Maya: Yes, we surface KV cache hit rate and why a cache miss occurred (e.g., different prompt prefix or cache cold start). Note, the KV names sometimes get garbled in transcription here, but in the UI they're precise.
[01:41] [01:40] Speaker 1: Uh hmm
[01:43] Maya: Example: here's a request that had a 450ms model time but 1.8s end-to-end because of batching queuing. The trace shows the queue wait, the batching window, and the kernel fallback to a quantized variant under load.
[01:58] Rae: That fallback is the thing we worry about — do you flag quality regressions when fallback happens?
[02:03] Maya: Yes, we have a fallback flag and a linked evaluation snapshot. If quality drops beyond a threshold we alert and you can see which prompts were affected. We also store the model rollouts so you can correlate with config changes.
[02:15] Tom: On the security side, can we redact prompt text in logs? Our prompts contain PII.
[02:21] Jordan: Good question. We support masking and configurable retention. You can set redaction rules at ingestion or on the UI side for different roles. Full text is available to users with appropriate RBAC and audit trails.
[02:33] Maya: I can show the audit log quickly — here's an access event, who viewed what, and we can export CSVs for compliance.
[02:41] Samir: Nice. Are the logs stored in our VPC for Private deployments? We prefer not to have logs leave our network.
[02:48] Maya: For Private, logs can remain in your VPC or on-prem store; we integrate with S3/GCS with encryption keys you control. Hosted mode stores logs in Redwood-managed storage with retention settings.
[02:59] Lena: That works. What's typical retention policy? 90 days? 180?
[03:04] Jordan: Default is 90, enterprise tiers can go to 1, 3 years; custom retention and cold storage options exist. We'll send the exact SOC2 doc and retention matrix.
[03:12] [03:10] Speaker 2: mmhm
[03:15] Maya: Back to the trace — here's an error-analysis view. We group errors by root cause heuristics: model hallucination, rate-limit/timeouts, downstream enrichment failures, or parsing exceptions. You can filter and pin sample requests to build repro prompt sets.
[03:31] Samir: That's useful — we spend a lot of time triaging hallucinations. Can we run automated repro tests against a committed prompt set?
[03:39] Maya: Yes, the Console supports eval runs against pinned prompt sets; you can schedule nightly runs and get regressions alerts. It writes results to the project and can be tied to rollouts.
[03:49] Rae: Will that work on Dedicated capacity too? Our plan is to eventually move to Dedicated.
[03:54] Maya: Absolutely — evals and tracing work across Hosted and Dedicated. For Dedicated we provide additional metrics about GPU utilization and kernel-level timings.
[04:05] Jordan: Let's walk through a specific debugging flow. Maya, show the failing request Samir mentioned in the prep notes.
[04:12] Maya: Pulling it up now — request ID nf-20260301-88a. You can see the timeline: user prompt -> enrichment call to external doc store -> model call -> post-processing. The error happened during enrichment (timeout) then we attempted fallback to cached response which produced stale output.
[04:30] Samir: Exactly, that was the one. The enrichment service is flaky under load. How does Redwood present root cause?
[04:36] Maya: We annotate each span. The enrichment call had a 504 and bucketed as downstream failure. The Console flags it and suggests remediation: increase enrichment timeout, enable async enrichment or configure graceful degradation routes.
[04:50] Lena: Can we set policy to always return partial outputs instead of failing the whole request?
[04:55] Maya: Yes, you can set fallback policies per route — partial outputs, default-canned answer, or synthetic enrichment using cached embeddings. Policies are versioned so you can A/B or canary them.
[05:06] Tom: How are request logs protected? Is the access logged for auditors?
[05:10] Jordan: Every access is an audit event. We also support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and granular RBAC roles so you can limit who sees full prompt text.
[05:19] Samir: Great. Another ask — can we export the request logs to our SIEM in near real-time? We use Datadog and Splunk.
[05:26] Maya: We have webhook and streaming exports, plus connectors for Datadog and Splunk. Exports can be filtered by project, severity, or tag.
[05:34] [05:33] Speaker 3: okay
[05:36] Jordan: Next, performance debugging — here's the request logs view with histograms for latency by model variant. You can correlate tokens consumed, kernel selection, and the underlying hardware — e.g., A100 vs T4 or quantized CPU fallback.
[05:52] Samir: Useful. Often we see big variance in tail latency in production — can we alert on p95/p99 anomalies?
[05:58] Maya: Yes, anomaly detection hooks are built-in; you can send alerts to slack/email/pager for thresholds or z-score anomalies.
[06:06] Rae: Is there a cost view tied to traces? We want to see which requests cost the most.
[06:11] Maya: Yep, token-level cost breakdown is shown per request and aggregated by route/model. That helps find expensive prompts.
[06:18] Samir: On the topic of kernel fallbacks — does Redwood automatically choose quantized variants when under high load? We care about quality impact.
[06:26] Maya: We do have smart routing and model variant fallbacks. The Console shows a delta in eval scores for the variant; you can set thresholds that prevent fallback if quality drops too much. There's also an option to route to a cheaper variant only for background jobs.
[06:40] Tom: For compliance, we need to know key management. Are customer keys supported?
[06:44] Jordan: Yes, KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted can use customer-managed keys in VPC-link scenarios. We'll share the KMS matrix in the docs.
[06:55] Maya: Back to a debugging example — let's simulate a side-by-side of two requests: one that succeeded and one that failed. You can diff the traces: see different enrichment call latencies and an extra retry on the failing one. The diff highlights the span with 504.
[07:12] Samir: That diff view would really speed up triage. Do you store full payloads for diffs?
[07:17] Maya: By default we store truncated payloads, but enterprise customers can enable full payload retention with stronger controls and encryption.
[07:26] Rae: Any limits on storage size? We might want to keep a year of logs.
[07:30] Jordan: For Private deployments you can manage retention. For hosted, we offer long-term cold storage but it's an additional add-on. We'll put the retention pricing in the follow-up.
[07:40] [07:38] Speaker 4: yeah
[07:44] Maya: Quick note about real-time debugging — we have a live inspector where you can replay a request against different model variants or config changes. That helps validate fixes without re-sending traffic.
[07:55] Lena: Can replay be run against a replica of our production environment? We want to avoid test-state leakage.
[08:01] Maya: Replays can be sandboxed. For Dedicated/Private we can run replay against a snapshot instance. We also support synthetic replay with redacted PII.
[08:12] Samir: Ok good. Onboarding: how long to set up tracing and get meaningful data? We have a prod-like traffic spike pattern we want to capture.
[08:20] Jordan: Minimal integration is a lightweight SDK to annotate spans; full request-level tracing is maybe a day of work for a small team. For deeper enrichment traces you may need to add a couple of hooks. We provide templates.
[08:33] Rae: Who owns the SDK integration? Would your SEs help?
[08:36] Maya: Our SE team will help with an initial integration during the pilot; we typically do a 2-3 call onboarding including a short bench run.
[08:45] Samir: Bench run — can we run a throughput test for 100 req/s and watch fallback behavior?
[08:50] Maya: Yes, we can spin up a benchmark on Dedicated or Hosted to simulate that and show kernel fallbacks, batching effects, and KV performance.
[08:59] Jordan: Let's talk about next steps — we heard: security docs, pricing, benchmark slot. Anything else?
[09:06] Tom: I'd like to get a short writeup on how audit logs and RBAC map to our SOC2 controls.
[09:12] Jordan: We'll include that in the packet.
[09:15] Maya: Also, Samir wanted to provide sample failing request IDs so we can repro during the bench.
[09:21] Samir: I'll put those in the thread after this call.
[09:24] Rae: And send a short video clip of the trace diff view for our team to review.
[09:29] Jordan: Will do.
[09:31] [09:30] Speaker 1: okay thanks
[09:33] Maya: Any last technical Qs?
[09:35] Lena: One more — do you support exporting telemetry to our internal metrics pipeline? We use Prometheus for custom metrics.
[09:41] Maya: Yes, metrics exporters are available; we can push metrics to Prometheus exporters in your VPC for Dedicated/Private. Hosted can push to customer endpoints with sharding.
[09:52] Samir: Great. That covers it for me.
[09:55] Jordan: Excellent. Before we close, quick recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO summary, KMS matrix, retention/pricing, and set up a 30-min benchmark slot next week. Maya will share the tracing runbook and a demo workspace link. Samir will share failing request IDs and a short prompt set.
[10:18] Rae: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:21] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up in an email with docs and calendar invites. Bye.

Meeting end.
